```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r readModelDb("Serkland_2026_ocrelizumab")()$meta$reference`
* Description: `r readModelDb("Serkland_2026_ocrelizumab")()$meta$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-026-01692-8>

Serkland 2026 developed a population PK-PD model of ocrelizumab, an anti-CD20
monoclonal antibody, from serum concentrations and CD19+ lymphocyte counts
collected over 24 weeks after each of the first two 600 mg infusions in
newly diagnosed relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS). The model was
fitted in Monolix 2023R1 (SAEM).

Three candidate structures are reported (Supplementary Table S1). The final
model, packaged here, is "model 1 without TMDD" (Table 2):

```
dC/dt = -Q/V1 * C + Q/V1 * P - CL/V1 * C          (Eq. 5 without the CLT0 * B term)
dP/dt =  Q/V2 * C - Q/V2 * P                       (Eq. 6)
dB/dt =  B0 * kout - kdeg * C * B - kout * B,  B(0) = B0   (Eq. 12)
```

`C` and `P` are ocrelizumab concentrations (mg/L) in the central and
peripheral compartments and `B` is the CD19+ lymphocyte count per mm^3. The
drug removes B cells through a second-order term `kdeg * C * B` (the paper's
"irreversible binding approximation"), and production is fixed so that the
untreated count stays at the individual's observed baseline `B0`. Ocrelizumab
elimination does not depend on the B-cell count in the final model.

In the packaged model the paper's `kdeg` is named `kirrev` (log-scale
`lkirrev`), because `kdeg` in nlmixr2lib denotes a first-order degradation
rate constant (1/time), while this parameter is a second-order constant in
L/(day*mg). The observed baseline count is supplied as the covariate
`BLBCELL`.

# Population

Eleven treatment-naive adults with newly diagnosed RRMS (8 female, 3 male;
mean age 36 years, range 22-50; mean weight 73 kg, range 61-96; mean height
169 cm) from the ROS-MS sub-study of the Norwegian OVERLORD-MS trial received
ocrelizumab 600 mg as an approximately 4-hour IV infusion every 6 months
(Serkland 2026 Methods and Table 1). Samples were taken before and within
30 min after the infusion and at 2, 4, 8, 12 and 24 weeks after each of the
first two infusions (114 serum samples). Mean baseline CD19+ count was
297 per mm^3 (range 127-726). Ocrelizumab was measured by LC-MS/MS (LLOQ
4 ug/mL); CD19+ counts reported as zero were treated as censored below
7 per mm^3. Age, weight, BMI and sex were screened as covariates and none was
retained.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Serkland_2026_ocrelizumab")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lvc` (V1) | log(2.58 L) | Table 2 |
| `lvp` (V2) | log(1.95 L) | Table 2 |
| `lcl` (CL) | log(0.153 L/day) | Table 2 |
| `lq` (Q) | log(0.220 L/day) | Table 2 |
| `lkout` (kout) | fixed(log(0.02 1/day)) | Table 2 (fixed to the Pan et al. estimate; Results) |
| `lkirrev` (paper `kdeg`) | log(1.70 L/(day*mg)) | Table 2 |
| `etalvc` | 0.138^2 = 0.019044 | Table 2 (omega V1, SD) |
| `etalvp` | 0.109^2 = 0.011881 | Table 2 (omega V2, SD) |
| `etalcl` | 0.234^2 = 0.054756 | Table 2 (omega CL, SD) |
| `addSd` | 0.545 mg/L | Table 2 (sigma add,OCR) |
| `propSd` | 0.0662 | Table 2 (sigma prop,OCR) |
| `addSd_Bcell` | 2.28 per mm^3 | Table 2 (sigma add,CD19+) |
| Combined error form `(a + b*C) * e` | `combined1()` | Supplementary Material 2, Eq. 1 |
| `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(peripheral1)` | n/a | Eq. 5-6 with the target-mediated term removed (Sect. 2.4.1, Results) |
| `d/dt(bcell)`, `kin = BLBCELL * kout`, `bcell(0) = BLBCELL` | n/a | Eq. 10 and Eq. 12 |
| Log-normal IIV on V1, V2, CL only | n/a | Results ("random effects on CL, V1, and V2"); Supplementary Material 2 |

# Typical-patient profile over two infusions

A typical patient with the cohort-mean baseline count (297 per mm^3) receives
600 mg over 4 hours on day 0 and day 182 (the 6-monthly schedule).

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("Serkland_2026_ocrelizumab")
mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

inf_rate <- 600 / (4 / 24) # mg/day for a 4-h infusion
dose_times <- c(0, 182)

make_events <- function(ids, obs_times, dose_times, blbcell) {
  dose_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = dose_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 600, rate = inf_rate, evid = 1L, cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    dplyr::left_join(tibble::tibble(id = ids, BLBCELL = blbcell), by = "id") |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    as.data.frame()
}

obs_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 364, by = 1), 4 / 24, 182 + 4 / 24)))
ev_typ <- make_events(1L, obs_grid, dose_times, blbcell = 297)
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, events = ev_typ, returnType = "data.frame")
```

```{r typical-plot, fig.height = 6}
sim_typ |>
  dplyr::select(time, Cc, Bcell) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "output", values_to = "value") |>
  dplyr::mutate(output = dplyr::recode(output,
    Cc = "Ocrelizumab (mg/L)", Bcell = "CD19+ lymphocytes (per mm^3)"
  )) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, pmax(value, 1e-3))) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~output, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = NULL,
    title = "Typical patient, 600 mg every 182 days, baseline 297 per mm^3",
    caption = "Compare with the observed profiles in Figure 1 of Serkland 2026."
  )
```

Figure 1A of the paper shows observed peak concentrations after each infusion
of roughly 170-300 mg/L and troughs just before the second infusion of roughly
0.7-2 mg/L. The typical prediction lies inside the peak range and somewhat
below the observed troughs, in line with the paper's own individual fit
(Figure 2A, which predicts about 0.06 mg/L at day 187 against an observation
of about 0.8 mg/L).

```{r typical-check}
typ_cmax1 <- max(sim_typ$Cc[sim_typ$time <= 10])
typ_cmax2 <- max(sim_typ$Cc[sim_typ$time >= 182 & sim_typ$time <= 192])
typ_trough <- sim_typ$Cc[sim_typ$time == 182]
knitr::kable(
  tibble::tibble(
    Quantity = c("Peak after infusion 1 (mg/L)", "Peak after infusion 2 (mg/L)", "Concentration at day 182 (mg/L)"),
    Typical = signif(c(typ_cmax1, typ_cmax2, typ_trough), 3),
    `Figure 1A (observed)` = c("about 170-300", "about 170-300", "about 0.7-2")
  ),
  caption = "Typical-patient predictions against the observed ranges read from Figure 1A."
)
# Peak = dose / V1 less the small amount cleared during the 4-h infusion; a
# wrong V1, dose unit or infusion rate moves this far outside the observed
# 170-300 mg/L band.
stopifnot(typ_cmax1 > 170, typ_cmax1 < 300)
```

# Virtual cohort and stochastic profiles

A virtual cohort of 200 patients is simulated over the same two-infusion
schedule. Individual baseline CD19+ counts are drawn from a log-normal
distribution (median 270 per mm^3, geometric SD 0.45) truncated to the
observed range 127-726 per mm^3, which reproduces the Table 1 mean of about
297 per mm^3.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2026)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)
n_sub <- 200
draw_b0 <- function(n) {
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    x <- exp(rnorm(n, log(270), 0.45))
    out <- c(out, x[x >= 127 & x <= 726])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}
b0_cohort <- draw_b0(n_sub)
obs_grid_vpc <- sort(unique(c(
  0, 4 / 24, 1, 3, 7, 14, 21, 28, 42, 56, 84, 112, 140, 168, 182,
  182 + c(4 / 24, 1, 3, 7, 14, 21, 28, 42, 56, 84, 112, 140, 168, 182)
)))
ev_vpc <- make_events(seq_len(n_sub), obs_grid_vpc, dose_times, blbcell = b0_cohort)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ev_vpc[, c("id", "time", "evid")]))
sim_vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_vpc, returnType = "data.frame")
mean(b0_cohort)
```

```{r vpc-plot, fig.height = 6}
sim_vpc |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, Bcell) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Cc, Bcell), names_to = "output", values_to = "value") |>
  dplyr::group_by(output, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(value, 0.05), Q50 = median(value), Q95 = quantile(value, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(output = dplyr::recode(output,
    Cc = "Ocrelizumab (mg/L)", Bcell = "CD19+ lymphocytes (per mm^3)"
  )) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, pmax(Q50, 1e-3))) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(Q05, 1e-3), ymax = pmax(Q95, 1e-3)), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~output, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = NULL,
    title = "Simulated 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles (200 virtual patients)",
    caption = "Model-predicted profiles; compare with Figure 1 and Supplementary Figure 1 of Serkland 2026."
  )
```

The simulated CD19+ counts drop to near zero within days of each infusion and
start to recover towards the end of the 6-month interval in the patients with
the fastest ocrelizumab clearance, as observed in three of the eleven patients
(Figure 1B).

# Replicate Figure 3: time to B-cell repopulation for patient ID1

Figure 3A of the paper simulates 1000 virtual patients from the population
distribution with the baseline count of patient ID1 (`B0 = 144` per mm^3),
after a single 600 mg infusion, and reads off the day on which each
trajectory exceeds the repopulation threshold of 10 per mm^3. The 5th, 50th
and 95th percentile trajectories in Figure 3A cross the threshold at about
168, 236 and 345 days (digitised by the maintainers from the crossings of the
dashed and solid blue lines with the red threshold line). Here 200 virtual
patients are simulated.

```{r fig3}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(144)
n_fig3 <- 200
ev_fig3 <- make_events(seq_len(n_fig3), seq(0, 500, by = 1), 0, blbcell = 144)
sim_fig3 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_fig3, returnType = "data.frame")

cross_day <- sim_fig3 |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 20) |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(day = dplyr::first(time[Bcell >= 10]), .groups = "drop")

fig3_published <- c(Q05 = 168, Q50 = 236, Q95 = 345)
fig3_sim <- quantile(cross_day$day, c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95), na.rm = TRUE)
fig3_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  Percentile = c("5th", "50th", "95th"),
  Simulated = as.numeric(fig3_sim),
  `Figure 3A (digitised)` = as.numeric(fig3_published),
  `Difference (%)` = round(100 * (as.numeric(fig3_sim) / fig3_published - 1), 1)
)
knitr::kable(fig3_tab, caption = "Day on which CD19+ count first exceeds 10 per mm^3 after one 600 mg infusion, B0 = 144 per mm^3.")

# Centre and robust tails only, never the extremes. The crossing day is driven
# by the CL draw. With 3000 patients the model's own percentiles are about 155,
# 224 and 321 days (two seeds), i.e. 5-8% below the digitised values. With 200
# patients the SE of the median is about 2% and of the 5th/95th percentiles
# about 5%, so the bounds sit 3 SE beyond the model-true offset. A misread kout
# or kdeg, or a dose-unit error, moves the median by far more than 12%.
stopifnot(
  sum(is.na(cross_day$day)) <= 0.1 * n_fig3,
  abs(fig3_tab$`Difference (%)`[2]) < 12,
  all(abs(fig3_tab$`Difference (%)`[c(1, 3)]) < 25)
)
```

```{r fig3-plot}
sim_fig3 |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Bcell, 0.05), Q50 = median(Bcell), Q95 = quantile(Bcell, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time)) +
  geom_line(data = sim_fig3, aes(y = Bcell, group = id), colour = "grey75", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q50), colour = "blue") +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q05), colour = "blue", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q95), colour = "blue", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 10, colour = "red", linetype = "dotdash") +
  labs(
    x = "Day", y = "CD19+ lymphocyte count (per mm^3)",
    title = "Figure 3A: 200 virtual patients, B0 = 144 per mm^3",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3A of Serkland 2026."
  )
```

```{r fig3-hist}
ggplot(cross_day, aes(day)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 7, fill = "skyblue", colour = "black") +
  labs(
    x = "Day of first CD19+ count above 10 per mm^3", y = "Patients",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3C of Serkland 2026 (unweighted prior)."
  )
```

The crossing-day distribution agrees with Figure 3A and 3C, with the packaged
model crossing the threshold about 5-8% (10-25 days) earlier than the
digitised percentiles. The paper sampled 1000 patients and may also have
included residual or estimation uncertainty in its draws, which this
simulation does not. The vertical scale of
Figure 3A does not: its trajectories start from, and return towards, about
255 per mm^3 rather than the stated `B0 = 144` (see Assumptions and
deviations).

# PKNCA validation

Non-compartmental parameters for ocrelizumab are computed over each 182-day
dosing interval of the virtual cohort. The paper reports no NCA values, so the
check is internal: the terminal half-life PKNCA estimates from the simulated
profiles is compared with each patient's own analytic terminal (beta)
half-life from the two-compartment micro-constants. CD19+ counts are a
turnover response, not a drug concentration, and are not analysed by NCA.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim_vpc |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "600 mg every 182 days") |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, treatment, time)

dose_df <- ev_vpc |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "600 mg every 182 days") |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 182), end = c(182, 364),
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_df <- as.data.frame(nca_res)

nca_df |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast", "half.life")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(start, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median = signif(median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    p05 = signif(quantile(PPORRES, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    p95 = signif(quantile(PPORRES, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Interval = ifelse(start == 0, "Infusion 1 (day 0-182)", "Infusion 2 (day 182-364)")) |>
  dplyr::select(Interval, PPTESTCD, median, p05, p95) |>
  dplyr::rename("NCA parameter" = PPTESTCD, Median = median, "5th pct" = p05, "95th pct" = p95) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated NCA of ocrelizumab (units: mg/L, day, day*mg/L).")
```

```{r halflife-check}
indiv <- sim_vpc |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, cl, vc, vp, q) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    k10 = cl / vc, k12 = q / vc, k21 = q / vp,
    beta = 0.5 * ((k10 + k12 + k21) - sqrt((k10 + k12 + k21)^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)),
    thalf_analytic = log(2) / beta
  )
hl <- nca_df |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life", start == 0) |>
  dplyr::select(id, thalf_nca = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(indiv, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (thalf_nca / thalf_analytic - 1))
summary(hl$thalf_analytic)
summary(hl$pct_diff)
# Both sides use the same drawn parameters; the gap is PKNCA's choice of
# terminal points on a weekly-to-monthly grid, so a robust envelope applies.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(hl$pct_diff, na.rm = TRUE)) < 5,
  quantile(abs(hl$pct_diff), 0.9, na.rm = TRUE) < 15
)
```

The typical terminal half-life is
`r signif(log(2) / (0.5 * ((0.153/2.58 + 0.220/2.58 + 0.220/1.95) - sqrt((0.153/2.58 + 0.220/2.58 + 0.220/1.95)^2 - 4 * (0.153/2.58) * (0.220/1.95)))), 3)`
days, consistent with the roughly linear log-concentration decline over
days 50-180 in Figure 1A.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Final model only.** Supplementary Table S1 also reports "model 1 with
  TMDD" (target-mediated elimination `CLT0 * C * B` with `CLT0` and `kout`
  fixed; unstable estimation) and "model 2" (an Emax stimulation of B-cell
  loss, "drastically worse model fit"). Both are model-development candidates
  and are not packaged; the paper's final model is Table 2.
- **Parameter name.** The paper's `kdeg` (L/(day*mg)) is packaged as
  `kirrev`, the name already used in nlmixr2lib for a second-order
  irreversible drug-by-target loss term (`Papasouliotis_2022_evobrutinib`).
  The value is unchanged.
- **Equation 8 typesetting.** The printed simplified PK equation (Eq. 8)
  shows `Q/V2 * P` as the return term of the central compartment, whereas
  Eq. 3 and Eq. 5 show `Q/V1 * P`. Only `Q/V1 * P` conserves mass for
  concentrations `C` and `P`; the packaged model uses the standard
  two-compartment amount form, which is equivalent to Eq. 3/5.
- **Baseline count.** The final model uses each patient's observed baseline
  count without a random effect (Eq. 10). For simulation the user supplies it
  as `BLBCELL`. The paper used the population median for two patients with a
  missing baseline.
- **Infusion.** Doses are simulated as 600 mg over 4 hours, the approximate
  infusion duration stated in the Methods. The trial gave 600 mg as a single
  infusion every 6 months; the label's split first dose (2 x 300 mg two weeks
  apart) is not part of this data set.
- **Censoring.** CD19+ counts reported as zero were fitted with the M3 method
  at a quantification limit of 7 per mm^3. This is part of the estimation, not
  of the model; simulated `Bcell` values are uncensored.
- **Figure 3A vertical scale.** The caption states `B0 = 144` per mm^3 for
  patient ID1, and simulating with 144 gives threshold-crossing days within
  5-8% of Figure 3A and the histogram of Figure 3C. The plotted trajectories,
  however, start from and recover towards about 255 per mm^3, which is not
  possible with `B0 = 144` because the model's steady state is `B0`.
  Simulating with `B0 = 255` matches the plateau but moves the median
  crossing about 30 days earlier (to about 200 days, against about 236 in the
  figure). The two cannot both hold
  for the published model; the caption value is used here.
- **Model code not available.** The paper states that the Monolix files and
  R scripts are deposited at Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.17184648). That DOI
  did not resolve when this model was packaged (2026-11-18), so the model is
  built from the printed equations and Table 2.
- No erratum or correction notice was found for this article as of
  2026-11-18.
